questions.explanation: A precise definition prevents the caricature from slipping back in. Global justice debates whether principles of justice extend beyond domestic society. This is the position defended by John Rawls. The claim that global justice holds that existing states are the only units of justice is a common mistake about the view, often described as "statist conflation of global justice". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: the scope of justice is contested. The distinction between the view and its caricature is what the question tests.
